title: Exact-bitmap BF pushed through CM compress offset
hypothesis: FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp:1059) builds a BF only when pushdown_column.storage_offset.IsNull() && !has_cast. When compressed materialization compresses a join key (__internal_compress_integral_*(x, off)), the probe scan gets min/max only. E0019 showed that in q04 the lineitem probe then stays at ~37.9M rows when ~2.3M would match. A previous run on this codebase measured the same blockage on q09: an exact-bitmap BF (the bitmap is built over the compressed HT keys, and the probe subtracts off before lookup) cut the orders scan from 15M to 2.94M rows, q09 -9..-14%, over two separate ports. The hashed BF variant was bench +4.7%, so use only the exact mode, where the offset shift is a trivial and safe integer subtraction.
plan: 1) src/include/duckdb/planner/filter/bloom_filter.hpp: add `uint64_t key_offset = 0` (with SetKeyOffset) to BFTableFilter, and make the copy, equality and serialization paths carry it. 2) src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp: in the exact-mode probe paths (the IsExact branches at ~177/229/337), subtract key_offset from the raw storage value before the range and bit test. Do this in the integer domain the exact-range check already uses, and test that value < off, or the subtraction underflowing, maps to 'not present'. Use HUGEINT or a wraparound-safe compare. 3) physical_hash_join.cpp FinalizeFilters: add a second branch for !has_cast-equivalent integral types, when storage_offset is non-null and join_condition==0. Call TrySetExactBloomFilter with the RAW (compressed, unshifted) min/max of the HT keys, not the offset-shifted values used for the min/max filters. Push the BF only if bf.IsExact() succeeded, and set key_offset = storage_offset cast to uint64. Never push a hashed BF through an offset. Note that has_cast is true here, because condition type (compressed UINTEGER etc.) != storage type. Gate on storage_offset non-null plus both types integral instead of !has_cast. 4) Keep deferred_bloom_filters handling identical to the existing branch. Verify on q04/q09 with EXPLAIN ANALYZE: the probe scan should show a BF and lower row counts. For correctness, compare counts with SET disabled_optimizers='join_filter_pushdown', including a key range that starts at a non-zero offset (CM only fires when the est. build is >=1M rows, so test tables need ~15M rows).
expected_gain: q09 -9..-14% (prior measured), q04 -5..-15% (lineitem probe 37.9M→~2.3M rows), possibly q03/q05/q18 a few %. Geomean ~-1.5..-2.5%.
generality: Any hash join on dense integer keys where an aggregate, sort or large-join materialization causes CM to compress the key. This is common for FK/PK joins on large fact tables. Joins with unselective builds may pay a BF probe cost, but the existing selectivity auto-disable covers that.
risk: Medium. If the offset sign or underflow is handled wrongly, rows get pruned incorrectly and results are wrong, so test with a shifted key range. Header change to BFTableFilter.
